Ukl men, healed by camels' milk and urine, kill the shepherd, take the camels and leave Islam; caught, they have hands and feet cut, eyes seared, and die without water.
A man rebukes the Prophet for giving Ali's gold to four chiefs; the Prophet foretells among his offspring Quran reciters who leave the religion like an arrow and kill Muslims.
Sparing Dhul-Khuwaisira who demanded justice, the Prophet foretold people whose Quran does not pass their throats, who leave Islam like an arrow; Ali fought them and found the man described.
A Christian convert who wrote for the Prophet returned to Christianity, saying the Prophet knew only what he wrote; three times the earth threw out his body after burial.
People of Ukl and Uraina accept Islam, then revert, kill the Prophet's shepherd and drive off the camels; caught, their eyes are branded and hands and legs cut off.
Rebuked over sharing Ali's gold among four, the Prophet refuses Khalid's request to kill the man and foretells people from his offspring who recite the Quran but leave the religion.
The Prophet shared something among four men to win their hearts; a man accused him of injustice, and he said the man's offspring would produce people who renounce the religion.
The Prophet foretells people who recite the Quran without it passing their throats and who go out of Islam like an arrow through game; Ali's report says to kill them.
Men of Ukl and Uraina, given camels' milk and urine to drink, reverted to disbelief, killed the shepherd and took the camels; their eyes were branded and hands cut off.
Told by Dhul Khawaisira to act justly, the Prophet foretold seemingly devout men who would leave Islam like an arrow, marked by a deformed-handed man found among those Ali fought.
Ukl men cured by camels' milk and urine turned renegades, killed the shepherd, took the camels; their hands and feet were cut, eyes branded, and they were left to die.
Ibn Abbas cited the Prophet's order to kill, not burn, whoever changes his religion; Mu'adh insisted a man reverting to Judaism be killed; Abu Bakr resolved to fight Zakat refusers.
The Prophet foretold people whose Quran recital never passes their throats, who leave the religion like an arrow through game, and said to kill them; Ali killed them.
Seeing a man who had become Muslim then reverted to Judaism, Mu'adh refused to sit unless he were killed, calling it the verdict of Allah and His Apostle.
When some Arabs reverted to disbelief after the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr insisted, against Umar's doubt, on fighting those who separated zakat from prayer, and Umar saw he was right.
A man rebuked the Prophet's gold gifts to Najd chiefs; the Prophet foretold the man's offspring would include Quran reciters who leave Islam like an arrow and kill Muslims.
People will come from the East reciting the Quran without it passing their throats, leaving the religion like an arrow never to return; their sign is shaving.
